title: Godzilla Dev: GTA 6 Was Never Part of Our Thinking for Release Date
description: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered and GTA 6 both launch this November, but the dev team says Rockstar's game never influenced their release date.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## Godzilla Devs Unfazed by November Showdown with GTA 6

In the modern video game industry, steering clear of Rockstar Games' massive releases is standard practice for many developers. The looming shadow of a blockbuster like *Grand Theft Auto VI* usually sends competing titles scrambling for safer release windows. Yet, every so often, a developer decides to march to the beat of their own drum.

According to a recent report by IGN Games, *Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered* is scheduled to launch this November, placing it squarely in the same release window as GTA 6. Despite the immense market dominance and inevitable cultural footprint of Rockstar's upcoming open-world epic, the team behind the arena fighter has revealed that Rockstar's latest was "never part of our thinking" when they chose their release date.

## Sticking to the Core Vision

While sharing a launch month with one of the most anticipated entertainment products in history might sound daunting to some, the Godzilla development team remains focused on their own project's trajectory. By prioritizing their specific niche—arena fighting and classic monster combat—they are catering to a distinct audience whose gaming preferences may differ from the typical open-world demographic.

Whether this fearless scheduling strategy pays off or gets entirely overshadowed by the GTA 6 hype train remains to be seen. However, it highlights a refreshing approach where a studio bases its milestones on internal readiness rather than external industry panic.

## Editor's Take

It is refreshing to see a development team unaffected by the gravitational pull of GTA 6. While sales figures will inevitably favor Rockstar, *Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered* knows its audience and is sticking to its own schedule. Sometimes, focusing on your own game is the best strategy of all.
